seg_membrane_chord_score — EMPROOF suspect op

• Data kinds: labels2d × image2d → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.seg_membrane_chord_score(labels, membrane, tau: 'float' = 0.2, band: 'int' = 4, min_area: 'int' = 1500, min_segment: 'int' = 20, normalize: 'bool' = True, ignore_zero: 'bool' = True, max_points: 'int' = 400, min_hole: 'int' = 4) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import emproof; emproof.seg_membrane_chord_score(labels, membrane, tau: 'float' = 0.2, band: 'int' = 4, min_area: 'int' = 1500, min_segment: 'int' = 20, normalize: 'bool' = True, ignore_zero: 'bool' = True, max_points: 'int' = 400, min_hole: 'int' = 4) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsemproof.get("seg_membrane_chord_score"))

Usage

Suspected merge: length of the membrane "chord" crossing the interior of a label / diameter of the label. One row per label (connected component).

Procedure: Make pixels with membrane response > tau inside the component (within band px from the boundary) into 8 connected components, For each membrane component greater than or equal to min_segment px, thicken it by 3 px to the boundary side (distance ≤ band + 3) The chord length is the distance between the two farthest pixels that can be touched. score = max chord length / sqrt(area). A membrane that connects two boundaries (= boundary between two pasted cells) has score ≈ 1, and fragments that do not touch the boundary are 0 or small. Membrane component with holes (min_hole hole larger than px = closed ring = mitochondria/vesicles) is excluded from string candidates --- At two points on the boundary Since the touching rings have the same two distant points'' as the strings, we first divide them based on the presence or absence of holes. The membrane that has been cut into an arc is This cannot be excluded (the main reason why AUC does not reach 1 in real data).

CREMI sample A (12 cross sections of 512², prototype), artificial fusion component vs. others: AUC 0.83 (tau 0.2).

Columns: label / component / area / score / chord_px / n_segments / cy / cx (score descending order). Components less than min_area are not counted (small fragment chords will always come out higher as they are equal to the diameter).

>>> table = seg_membrane_chord_score(labels, seg_membrane_response(raw))

>>> table["label"][:5], table["score"][:5] # Most suspicious
